walkthroughs.body_html:
Component 03/04: Listening and Appraising — a core area of A-Level Music.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Component 03/04: Listening and Appraising brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Component 03/04: Listening and Appraising.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Whose 1973 Structure of Atonal Music codified set classes?
options: Forte
Lewin
Babbitt
Rahn

mcqs.q: Whose 1998 Classical Form defines thematic functions?
options: Caplin
Hepokoski
Webster
Rosen
Music played in a circle.
It is always C major.
A round where voices enter at different times.
A recurring main theme (A) alternates with contrasting episodes (B, C, etc.).

mcqs.q: What happens in the recapitulation of sonata form?
options: Both subjects return, but the second subject is now in the tonic key.
The exposition is repeated exactly.
Entirely new material is introduced.
Music played in a circle.

mcqs.q: How do you identify a major key from its key signature?
options: The last sharp is the leading note (semitone below tonic); the second-to-last flat is the tonic.
Music played in a circle.
The number of sharps or flats equals the tonic note number.
It is always C major.
